headline: 40-year wait ends: Mexico beat Ecuador 2-0 to reach World Cup last 16
summary: The co-hosts broke a long-standing knockout stage 'curse' with goals from Julian Quinones and Raul Jimenez at a rocking Azteca Stadium.
details: Mexico secured a historic 2-0 victory over Ecuador on Tuesday, ending a 40-year drought of knockout stage wins at the World Cup. The win sends the co-hosts into the round of 16, sparking euphoric celebrations at the Azteca Stadium.

Julian Quinones opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a thunderous finish into the top corner. Raul Jimenez doubled the lead nine minutes later, netting his 47th international goal and moving closer to the all-time national scoring record.

The match was delayed by an hour due to thunderstorms, but over 80,000 fans filled the stadium in a sea of green. Mexico dominated the first half, which was described as one of their most complete performances of the tournament.

A notable highlight was 17-year-old Gilberto Mora, who became the youngest player to start a World Cup match since Pele. He received a standing ovation from the crowd when he was substituted later in the game.

Ecuador struggled to break through Mexico's disciplined defense, which has yet to concede a goal in the tournament. The match ended with Ecuador's Piero Hincapie receiving a red card in the closing stages.

Mexico will now face either England or the Democratic Republic of Congo in the last 16. The upcoming match will be played at the Azteca Stadium, marking the final game of the tournament hosted at this venue.
